newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN RUPEE WEAKENS MILDLY ON SBI'S DLR PURCHASE.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN RUPEE WEAKENS MILDLY ON SBI'S DLR PURCHASE.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakenend mildly in late morning Wednesday trade after the State Bank of India (SBI) stepped in to buy dollars, dealers said.
"SBI came in and bought upto 35.7250 levels," a dealer said.
The rupee opened the day at 35.715/720 against the dollar.
The spot rupee was quoted at 35.720/727 a dollar.
Forward premiums opened lower on lack of demand and there was little activity, dealers said.
"The spot rupee gave sphinx-like response to the Reserve Bank of India announcement on allowing offshore debt funds to cover forward," a European bank said in its India commentary.

"Forwards expectedly were pushed up by speculative paying. But given the quantum of funds invested in debt by offshore funds ($105 million), their impact on the forwards should be marginal," the bank said.
